lots.what_it_is: Taxidermy two-headed (dicephalic) calf, Hereford colouring, curled lying pose, about 56cm long, tail detached. No maker or date.

sold.note: Page opened. Two-headed calf HEAD mount only, 29cm, America early 20th c, 'excellent specimen', est USD 1,500-4,500, isSold true. Close, not same item (head mount, not whole body; US specialist market). Rate 1 USD = 1.52 AUD.
Page opened. Two-headed LAMB, 1900s, in glazed sideshow display case, est USD 400-600. Category guide only, not a calf. Rate 1.52.

lots.guide_summary: 1 close sold (US two-headed calf head mount, USD 1,600 = about AUD 2,430 at 1.52), plus 1 category-guide sold (two-headed lamb, same price) not counted in the range. No same-item whole-calf sale found and no Australian results. US oddity market is much deeper than the Australian one.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry survives (the calf sale is a head mount, the lamb is a different animal), so by the rules keep_max = 0 and flip_max = 0. For reference only: if the head mount were treated as same-item, keep = 2430/1.22 = 1991 -> 1990; flip = (2430 less 15% fees and about $80 freight = 1985)/2.44 = 813 -> 810. Not used as a limit.
lots.confidence_reason: No maker label to read, no same-item sold result, and genuineness (true dicephalic calf versus two heads grafted onto one skin) cannot be confirmed from photos.
lots.condition: Tail detached and lying loose. Flaking and loss to both muzzles and lips, wear to hooves. Coat looks reasonably full. No case.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 1-3: two complete heads sharing one neck and body, consistent in colour and hair direction, which is what a genuine dicephalic calf mount looks like. Photos 1-3: muzzle skin cracked and flaking on both heads. Photo 4: tail fully detached. Photo 5: body intact, no seams obvious from above. No labels, plaques or maker marks.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher had no entries. Earlier snippet-only items (2016 USD 15,000 eBay ask via boingboing, 2019 NZ two-headed goat ask) not used: no openable page. Two-headed chicken (LiveAuctioneers id 131751548, search card showed USD 375) not listed as the item page did not return data.
lots.question_for_armitage: Any provenance, age or taxidermist known? Can you confirm it is a genuine two-headed birth (one skin) rather than a composite, and can the tail be reattached? Any insect damage underneath?

lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maxima are 0.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 6: incised 'John Campbell Tas' in script and 'DIL' inside base, read by eye. Photo 5: clear hairline crack in corner. Photo 7: chips exposing buff body. Typical Campbell drip glaze.

lots.question_for_armitage: Does the corner crack go right through the wall (does it hold water)? Any other chips or restoration?
